title: NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission begins regulating providers (New South Wales)
summary: From 1 July 2018 the NDIS Commission replaced state arrangements for registering and regulating NDIS providers in New South Wales.

instruments.title: National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Quality and Safeguards Commission and Other Measures) Act 2017

commenced.what: NDIS Commission took over provider registration and regulation

direction_rationale: One national registration and practice standard can ease operating across states, but audit and registration costs fall hardest on small providers and may push them out or to unregistered supply.
comparison: Staggered start: NSW and SA 2018, other states 2019, WA December 2020
confounders: NDIS full-scheme rollout by region from 1 Jul 2016

verified.notes: Dates from the NDIS Commission's page on each state and territory.

assessment.summary: The national NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission replaced state regulation of disability service providers. One national registration eases operating across states, but audits and registration costs fall hardest on small providers, many of whom stay unregistered.

marks.reason: One national registration and practice standard replaced state and territory arrangements.
Registered providers face audits and verification whose cost weighs most on small providers.
Registration costs deter small providers from registering, narrowing who can serve some participants.

responsible.note: Administers the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013.
